ops.name: arch.arcade
ops.summary: A wall of repeating arched bays following a path — THE Roman building block. Stack these to turn a stadium bowl into a colosseum, or run one along a line for an aqueduct or a cloister. Bays are spaced by arc length so an oval colonnade stays even through the turns.

path.description: Flat [x0,y0,z0, ...] path; leave empty and use path_shape

straight.description: oval: length of each straight in metres

length.description: line: total length in metres along X

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile

bays.description: Number of arched openings around the path

height.description: Storey height in metres, plinth to cornice

opening.description: Fraction of each bay that is opening rather than pier (0.3-0.75)

arch_rise.description: Height of the arch semicircle; 0 makes it a true semicircle (half the opening width)

springing.description: Height where the arch starts, as a fraction of storey height

voussoirs.description: Segments per arch — 7 reads as an arch, more is wasted at distance

cornice_jut.description: How far the cornice projects past the wall

engaged_columns.description: Half-columns on the piers — the Colosseum's storey articulation

ops.name: arch.colonnade
ops.summary: A ring or run of free-standing columns with an entablature — temple fronts, stadium rims, forum porticos. Cheaper than an arcade and the right silhouette for a top storey.

path.description: Flat [x0,y0,z0, ...] path; leave empty and use path_shape

straight.description: oval: length of each straight in metres

length.description: line: total length in metres along X

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile

entablature.description: Depth of the beam carried across the tops; 0 for none

flutes.description: Fluted shafts (costs triangles, only reads up close)

statues.description: Blocky statue silhouettes above every fourth column

ops.name: arch.gateway
ops.summary: A monumental arched gate — the triumphal entrance every Roman venue frames its far end with. One big central arch, optional flanking arches, an attic storey above.

side_arches.description: Smaller arches either side of the main opening

attic.description: Attic storey height above the cornice; 0 for none

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile

ops.name: bake.transfer
ops.summary: Bake textures from a source mesh (the neural soup, the high-poly sculpt) onto a target mesh (the retopo'd game mesh) via selected-to-active projection: base colour and tangent-space normal map. This is the AAA high->low transfer step — the game mesh keeps the source's surface richness at a fraction of the triangles.

target.description: Target mesh object (retopo'd, with fresh UVs)

maps.description: Which maps to bake: base_color, normal, ao

ray_distance.description: Projection ray length in metres — raise if the bake misses recessed detail, lower if it picks up neighbouring parts

ops.name: build.array
ops.summary: Repeat an object along a vector, or in a 2D/3D grid. Fences, columns, pipes, city blocks, crowd props.

counts.description: Repeat count per axis, e.g. [5] or [4,4] or [3,3,2]

join.description: Merge into a single mesh (fewer draw calls)

ops.name: build.bevel
ops.summary: Chamfer an object's sharp edges. The single highest-impact polish step for hard-surface props.

angle.description: Only bevel edges sharper than this (degrees)

ops.name: build.box
ops.summary: Chamfered box. The chamfer is what makes a box read as a solid object under game lighting instead of a flat card.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

smooth.description: Smooth shading with a sharp-edge threshold

bevel_segments.description: Chamfer resolution (2 is plenty for game assets)

ops.name: build.cleanup
ops.summary: Weld duplicate vertices and optionally dissolve coplanar faces. Run before measuring or exporting.

dissolve_flat.description: Merge coplanar faces (cuts triangles, can create n-gons)

ops.name: build.cylinder
ops.summary: Cylinder, cone or truncated cone (set radius_top). Pillars, pipes, barrels, tent poles.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

smooth.description: Smooth shading (usually right for round shapes)

radius_top.description: Top radius; -1 means same as bottom, 0 makes a cone

segments.description: Radial segments — 12-16 is the game-asset sweet spot

ops.name: build.deform
ops.summary: Taper, twist or noise-displace a mesh. Turns generic primitives into things with character.

amount.description: taper: top scale factor. noise/jitter: displacement in metres. squash: Z scale

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: build.extrude
ops.summary: Inset-and-extrude faces selected by their normal direction. Makes panels, ledges, windows and recesses.

inset.description: Inset before extruding — this is what makes a panel not a spike

threshold.description: Normal alignment required to count as facing that direction

ops.name: build.greeble
ops.summary: Scatter panel detail across faces — sci-fi hulls, machinery, city blocks, tech walls. Deterministic for a given seed.

seed.description: Random seed; same seed gives the same result forever

density.description: Fraction of faces that get a panel (0..1)

cuts.description: Subdivision passes before panelling — more cuts, finer greeble

ops.name: build.lathe
ops.summary: Revolve a 2D profile into a solid. The highest value-per-parameter op here: bottles, vases, columns, goblets, chess pieces, tree trunks, fountains.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

profile.description: Flat [radius0, height0, radius1, height1, ...] pairs, bottom to top

ops.name: build.mirror
ops.summary: Mirror geometry across an axis. Halves the modelling work for anything symmetrical — characters, vehicles, buildings.

ops.name: build.plane
ops.summary: Flat quad, optionally grid-subdivided. Floors, walls, water, billboards, terrain bases.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

smooth.description: Smooth shading with a sharp-edge threshold

ops.name: build.prism
ops.summary: N-sided prism. Hex tiles, crystals, columns, low-poly trunks.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

smooth.description: Smooth shading with a sharp-edge threshold

ops.name: build.sphere
ops.summary: UV sphere or icosphere. Icospheres have even topology and are better bases for rocks and organic shapes.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

ops.name: build.subdivide
ops.summary: Subdivide all faces. Use sparingly — subdivision multiplies triangles fast.

ops.name: build.sweep
ops.summary: Sweep a 2D cross-section along a path — the workhorse for level geometry. Racetracks, grandstands, roads, ramparts, rails, tunnels, mouldings and pipes are all one profile plus one path. Frames use parallel transport, so a closed loop does not twist.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile

profile.description: Flat [lateral0, vertical0, lateral1, vertical1, ...] cross-section in metres, relative to the path

profile_scales.description: Flat [lateral0, vertical0, ...] multipliers applied to the cross-section ALONG the path, interpolated to fit. This is what turns a uniform tube into an anatomy — a barrel that swells at the girth, a neck that tapers to the poll. Give a few key values, not one per point

path.description: Flat [x0,y0,z0, x1,y1,z1, ...] path points; leave empty and use path_shape instead

straight.description: oval: length of each straight in metres

length.description: line: total length in metres along X

segments.description: Path resolution (per turn for an oval)

closed_path.description: Close the path into a loop (oval and circle are always closed)

closed_profile.description: Treat the cross-section as a closed outline (a solid tube) rather than an open strip

ops.name: build.torus
ops.summary: Torus. Rings, handles, hoops, portal frames.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

ops.name: build.wedge
ops.summary: Right-triangle prism. Ramps, roof sections, chamfer blockouts.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

smooth.description: Smooth shading with a sharp-edge threshold

ops.name: char.animate
ops.summary: Author a keyframed animation clip on a rig: idle, walk, run, attack, jump, death or wave. Real pose-to-pose keys at contact/passing frames, not sine-wave wiggle — the difference between a walk and a shuffle.

length.description: Clip length in frames (24 frames at 30 fps = 0.8 s)

amplitude.description: Motion scale — 0.6 is subtle, 1.4 is exaggerated

loop.description: Match the last frame to the first so the clip cycles

action_name.description: Action name (defaults to the clip name)

ops.name: char.attach
ops.summary: Parent a prop to a character bone — a sword to hand_r, a shield to hand_l, a helmet to head. Keeps the prop's own pivot, so it animates with the character.

keep_transform.description: Keep the prop exactly where it already is, ignoring offset/rotation

ops.name: char.bake_pose
ops.summary: Freeze a posed rig into the mesh vertices and drop the skin. Turns a char.rig + char.pose result into a plain static mesh that keeps the pose through export — for background figures, props and NPCs that never animate.

rig.description: Armature to delete afterwards (default: the one deforming this mesh; pass "" to keep it)

keep_groups.description: Keep the vertex groups after baking

ops.name: char.creature
ops.summary: Proportioned quadruped body (canine/equine/feline/generic) or hexapod (insect: scarab class, three leg stations). Pair with char.creature_rig and char.animate — walk/trot/gallop/graze for quadrupeds, tripod-gait walk for hexapods. Deterministic, data-API only, metres.

length.description: Body length in metres (chest-to-hip; abdomen-tip to head for insect)

shoulder.description: Shoulder height in metres (thorax height for insect)

plan.description: Body plan — quadruped proportions or the hexapod scarab class

eyes.description: Eye blobs: natural (dark), glow (emissive — the underworld signature, reads at any distance)

eye_color.description: Eye colour; glow reads best saturated (#39ff88 underworld, #ffb35a ember)

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: char.creature_rig
ops.summary: Build a quadruped armature (hips root, spine chain, neck/head, 2-segment tail, 3-bone legs at both stations) fitted to a char.creature body, and skin it with the same shell-constrained distance-falloff solve as char.rig.

length.description: Chest-to-hip length; 0 measures from the mesh bounds Y extent

shoulder.description: Shoulder height; 0 measures from the mesh bounds Z extent

plan.description: Body plan the rig assumes — match char.creature

falloff.description: Weight blend sharpness; higher is more rigid

ops.name: char.face
ops.summary: Give a char.humanoid head a readable face — brow ridge, nose wedge, chin — so a close-up review render reads as a person, not a box. Stylised readability, not realism. Geometry is welded into the body mesh and takes the head bone when skinned.

height.description: Character height; 0 measures the mesh bounds

eyes.description: Eye blobs: natural (dark), glow (emissive — underworld/monster signature, reads at any distance)

eye_color.description: Eye colour; glow eyes read best saturated (#39ff88 underworld, #ffb35a ember)

ops.name: char.gait
ops.summary: Synthesize a walk/trot/gallop cycle from the rig's OWN morphology: measure the leg chains, pick the gait by Froude number (v²/gL — the real biomechanical transition rule), compute swing angles and cadence from a target speed in m/s, and key the result with real footfall phase patterns. No hand-authored table — any body plan, any size, any speed.

rig.description: Armature object name (humanoid, quadruped, or hexapod rig)

speed.description: Target locomotion speed in metres per second — gait style and cadence derive from it

style.description: 'auto' selects by Froude number (walk < 0.55, trot < 2.0, else gallop/run)

length.description: Cycle length in frames; 0 computes it from the cadence

loop.description: Match the last frame to the first so the clip cycles

ops.name: char.hands
ops.summary: Upgrade a char.humanoid's block hands with readable fingers: four two-segment fingers with a relaxed curl plus a thumb, so a weapon grip or open hand reads at review distance. Welded into the body mesh; the hand bones own them when skinned.

height.description: Character height; 0 measures the mesh bounds

curl.description: Finger curl in radians-ish (0 flat, 0.8 fist); a relaxed read is ~0.35

ops.name: char.humanoid
ops.summary: Proportioned humanoid blockout using classic figure-drawing head ratios (7.5 realistic, 8 heroic, 4 chibi). ~1400 tris. Pair with char.rig and char.animate for a complete animated character.

detail.description: Limb cross-section segments (6-10 is the game range)

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: char.outfit
ops.summary: Fit an armour or clothing piece to a char.humanoid body: cuirass, pteruges skirt, greaves, bracers, helmet or round shield. Fit is derived from the body's own proportions, materials are perceptually distinct by construction (this is the anti 'brown blob' op), and pieces bone-parent to the rig when one exists so they animate with the character.

piece.description: What to fit. greaves and bracers come in pairs; robe is a full-length caster/priest garment, hood its matching cowl

height.description: Character height; 0 measures the mesh bounds

build.description: Proportions the fit assumes — match the char.humanoid build

material.description: Material family (defaults per piece: bronze for cuirass/greaves/helmet/shield, leather for pteruges/bracers). The families are deliberately far apart in colour and response — keep them that way

color.description: Override colour; stay clear of the other pieces' colours or check.materials will fail the set

gap.description: Clearance between body and armour in metres; raise for bulky bodies

seed.description: Random seed (reserved; current pieces are fully deterministic)

ops.name: char.pose
ops.summary: Set a static pose on a rig — T-pose, A-pose, sitting, or a custom per-bone rotation. Useful for reference renders and for fixing an import rest pose.

bones.description: custom only: {"bone_name": [rx, ry, rz], ...} in degrees

ops.name: char.rig
ops.summary: Build a humanoid armature fitted to a mesh and skin it with distance-falloff weights. Single 'hips' root, snake_case bone names, glTF/Godot-compatible. No GUI needed.

height.description: Character height; 0 measures it from the mesh bounds

build.description: Proportions the rig assumes — match char.humanoid

falloff.description: Weight blend sharpness; higher is more rigid

ops.name: check.asset
ops.summary: Run the studio's ADR 0006 asset rules against the open scene: naming, units, applied transforms, origins, UVs, budgets, bone conventions, collision, textures, glTF-safe shaders. Same checks as `just asset-validate`, but before you write the file.

ops.name: check.conformance
ops.summary: Score how well each object conforms to the set's (or a reference object's) style fingerprint. Names the exact axis that breaks coherence — palette drift, texel-density mismatch, density outlier, edge-treatment drift — with the op that fixes it. The art-director gate: run it over a whole pack before export.

reference.description: Conform to THIS object's fingerprint instead of the set median

texture_size.description: Texture resolution the texel-density figure assumes

ops.name: check.critique
ops.summary: Quality critique with specific, actionable findings: triangle-density hot spots, degenerate and n-gon faces, UV stretch, texel-density mismatch between objects, non-manifold edges, unused material slots. Pair it with render.contact_sheet — numbers plus eyes.

texture_size.description: Texture resolution the texel-density figures assume

ops.name: check.image
ops.summary: Measure an image instead of eyeballing it: luminance range, blown highlights, crushed blacks, contrast, saturation, dominant colours and subject coverage. Reading a render is slow and cannot tell 'the asset is wrong' from 'the render is over-lit'. These numbers can, in a fraction of the time.

path.description: PNG to analyse — a render, a contact sheet, or a baked texture

colors.description: How many dominant colours to report

background.description: Backdrop colour, excluded from subject stats

ops.name: check.materials
ops.summary: Measure whether an asset's materials are actually distinguishable — the '8 materials, all the same brown' failure that produces mud-blob characters. Reports every material's colour in CIELAB and the pairwise perceptual distance (ΔE); fails when several materials are perceptually identical or share one roughness/metallic signature.

objects.description: Objects whose materials to measure (empty = every mesh)

min_delta_e.description: Perceptual-separation floor in ΔE76. Below ~6 the difference is invisible in game; 12 is a safe bar for metal vs leather vs cloth

ops.name: check.palette
ops.summary: Measure an asset against the game's art bible: every material's base colour is mapped to the nearest palette family in CIELAB and must land within tolerance (ΔE76). This is executable art direction — the difference between 'assets that look generated' and 'assets that look like they belong to one game'.

objects.description: Objects whose materials to measure (empty = every mesh)

bible.description: Art bible name (see ART_BIBLES) or a JSON list of {"name", "hex"} entries

tolerance.description: Max distance to the nearest family in ΔE76 — 18 is strict, 26 is permissive

ops.name: check.silhouette
ops.summary: Score how readable an object's silhouette is from the standard game camera angles. A prop that fails here will not read at gameplay distance no matter how good its texture is.

samples.description: Rays per axis for the projected-area estimate

ops.name: check.style
ops.summary: Compute the style fingerprint of every mesh: area-weighted palette (in CIELAB), texel density, triangle density, hard-edge ratio, material count, UV coverage. This is the raw material of art direction — 'do these 40 assets look like one game' is unanswerable without it.

texture_size.description: Texture resolution the texel-density figure assumes

palette_size.description: Dominant colours to keep per object, area-weighted

ops.name: env.amphitheatre
ops.summary: A complete Roman venue in one call: raked cavea, podium, arched arcade storey, statued attic colonnade, vomitoria stair wedges, velarium masts, hanging banners and gateways. This is the difference between a stone bowl and the Colosseum — arches and vertical rhythm. Use shape='oval' for a circus/hippodrome, 'circle' for an amphitheatre.

straight.description: oval only: length of each straight in metres

arena_margin.description: Flat run-off between the arena edge and the podium wall

podium_height.description: Height of the solid wall between arena and first seats

tiers.description: Seating tiers (maenianum), separated by walkway walls

tier_depth.description: Depth of each tier in metres

arcade_height.description: Height of the arched storey crowning the stands; 0 for none

arcade_bays.description: Arch count; 0 auto-sizes to roughly one arch per 8 m

colonnade.description: Statued attic colonnade above the arcade

vomitoria.description: Stair wedges dividing the seating; 0 auto-sizes

masts.description: Velarium masts on the rim; 0 auto-sizes, -1 for none

gateways.description: Monumental arched gates cut through the podium

banners.description: Hanging banners between arcade bays; 0 auto-sizes

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: env.arena
ops.summary: Complete combat arena in one call: floor, tiered walls, entrance arches and corner towers. A whole playable space from a single op.

tiers.description: Spectator tiers stepping up behind the wall

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: env.camp
ops.summary: A complete Age-1 settlement in one call: central fire (stones, log teepee, live embers), A-frame shelters ringing it, a stockade perimeter with a gate opening, a well, and storage racks on a deterministic seeded layout. The homeland diorama, not a bag of props — the layout relationships (fire at the heart, shelters facing it, one way in) are what makes it read as a camp instead of a yard sale.

name.description: Object-name prefix for the camp's structures

radius.description: Palisade ring radius in metres; shelters sit at ~55% of it

gate_angle.description: Compass degrees the gate opening faces (0 = +X, 90 = +Y). The ONE way in — put it toward where threats should come from

ground.description: Flatten a dirt disc under the camp — helps dioramas; skip when the game supplies terrain

seed.description: Layout seed — same seed, same camp, forever

ops.name: env.cliff
ops.summary: Rock cliff wall or canyon face with stratified layers. Blocks sightlines and frames a play space without the cost of terrain.

strata.description: How pronounced the rock layering is

seed.description: Random seed

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile

ops.name: env.road
ops.summary: Road, path or river bed following a polyline, conformed to a terrain surface if given.

target.description: Terrain to drape onto (empty = flat at Z=0)

offset.description: Height above the surface, to avoid z-fighting

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: env.scatter
ops.summary: Scatter copies of an object over a surface with Poisson-ish spacing, aligned to the surface normal. The op that turns bare terrain into a forest, a rockfield or a graveyard.

target.description: Surface to scatter onto (empty = scatter on the Z=0 plane)

area.description: Scatter area in metres when there is no target

align_to_normal.description: 0 = always upright, 1 = fully follow the surface tilt

seed.description: Random seed

join.description: Merge into one mesh — critical for draw calls

ops.name: env.terrain
ops.summary: Heightfield terrain with fBm noise, optional plateaus and erosion-like smoothing. Deterministic across machines, so CI can regenerate and diff it.

scale.description: Noise frequency — lower is broader hills

flatten_center.description: Radius in metres of a flat buildable area at the origin

seed.description: Random seed

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile

ops.name: env.water
ops.summary: Water plane with a gentle wave mesh and a translucent material. Fills moats, lakes and canals.

level.description: Z height of the water surface

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: export.asset
ops.summary: One call: save the .blend master, export the GLB, write the .meta.json sidecar and render a contact sheet. The complete hand-off for a finished asset.

asset_id.description: snake_case asset identifier — names every output file

out_dir.description: Directory for the outputs (defaults to the session output dir)

ai_prompt.description: What the asset was asked for — recorded in provenance

contact_sheet.description: Also render a review contact sheet

strict.description: Block export on problems that would corrupt the import

gate.description: Run gameready.review before writing anything; a failed review blocks the hand-off. Set false only for deliberate blockouts

style.description: Art direction passed to gameready.review when gate=true

ops.name: export.blend
ops.summary: Save the .blend master. Under ADR 0006 the .blend is the committed source of truth and the GLB is a derived artefact — always save both.

pack_textures.description: Embed image textures in the .blend. A master links textures by RELATIVE path, so the moment it is copied into assets-source those links break and the committed master is useless — `just asset-validate` fails it on missing textures

ops.name: export.gltf
ops.summary: Export to GLB/glTF with an engine-specific preset. Checks for the things that silently break an import first — unapplied scale, missing UVs, procedural materials — and tells you rather than shipping a broken file.

format.description: Binary GLB (one file) or text glTF (separate assets)

draco.description: Draco mesh compression — smaller files, slower load, not all importers support it

strict.description: Fail on problems that would corrupt the import instead of warning

rename.description: Names to apply IN THE EXPORTED FILE ONLY, e.g. {"horse": "Horse", "m_coat": "Coat", "gallop": "Gallop"}. Game code often looks up nodes and materials by exact name, and those names break the studio's snake_case rule — this satisfies both without renaming the master

ops.name: export.meta
ops.summary: Write the .meta.json sidecar the studio asset pipeline requires — id, licence, provenance including AI-generation disclosure, budgets and policies. Without this, `just asset-validate` rejects the asset.

ai_tool.description: AI tool used — required for honest provenance

ai_model.description: Model that drove the generation, if any

ai_prompt.description: Prompt or intent that produced the asset

ops.name: gameready.atlas
ops.summary: Merge several objects into one mesh with one shared material and a repacked UV atlas. The most effective draw-call reduction available — a room of 20 props becomes 1 draw call.

material.description: Material preset for the merged result

ops.name: gameready.budget
ops.summary: Check the scene against a platform triangle/texture budget and say what to do about anything over. Run this before export, every time.

asset_class.description: What kind of asset this is

objects.description: Objects to check (empty = every mesh in the scene)

ops.name: gameready.collision
ops.summary: Generate a physics collision proxy. Convex hulls are what you want for anything a character walks into; box is cheapest; simplified trimesh is for concave shapes like arenas and rooms. Named <object>-convcol / <object>-col per the studio import convention. SKIP for hulls that ride inside a moving body: Godot imports the proxy as a StaticBody3D child, and a static collider inside a CharacterBody3D blocks its own vehicle.

ratio.description: simplified only: decimation ratio for the trimesh proxy

inflate.description: Grow the proxy by this many metres (stops geometry poking through)

ops.name: gameready.lod
ops.summary: Generate a level-of-detail chain by decimation. Ratios are chosen so each level roughly halves the triangle count, which is what LOD switching expects. Named <object>_lod1..N to match the studio import convention.

levels.description: Number of reduced levels to create

ratios.description: Explicit decimation ratios, e.g. [0.5, 0.25, 0.1]. Empty auto-generates

layout.description: Offset each LOD along X for side-by-side review

ops.name: gameready.optimize
ops.summary: One-call cleanup pass: weld doubles, drop degenerate faces, recalculate normals, and report what it saved. Safe to run on anything.

dissolve_flat.description: Merge coplanar faces — cuts triangles but can create n-gons

triangulate.description: Triangulate (engines do this anyway; useful for exact counts)

ops.name: gameready.pivot
ops.summary: Fix pivots and transforms across many objects at once — the two things engines get wrong on import and nobody notices until a prop spins about its ankle.

apply_transforms.description: Bake rotation and scale into the mesh

snap_to_ground.description: Move each object so its lowest point sits at Z=0

to_origin.description: Also move the object itself to (0,0,0). Required for a single-asset master file — the studio validator rejects a root object that is not at the world origin

ops.name: gameready.review
ops.summary: The quality gate: aggregate check.critique and check.materials into one pass/fail verdict before export. Exists because quality steps that are optional get skipped — a scene that passes this cannot ship the mud-blob failure (perceptually identical materials), broken geometry, or missing UVs without knowing it.

objects.description: Objects to review (empty = every mesh in the scene)

severity.description: Findings at this level or worse fail the gate. 'error' blocks only what corrupts or reads as broken; 'warn' also blocks advisories like texel-density spread

style.description: 'realistic' additionally fails an asset whose materials are ALL flat untextured colour — bake material.bake_pbr or pick the stylized look deliberately

min_delta_e.description: Material-separation floor in ΔE76, passed to check.materials

ops.name: gameready.socket
ops.summary: Add a named empty as an attachment socket — muzzle points, hardpoints, spawn markers, VFX anchors. Engines import empties as nodes you can query by name.

parent.description: Object to parent the socket to

ops.name: gameready.texture_budget
ops.summary: Measure what the textures actually cost in GPU memory and flag any over the platform's resolution cap. Triangle budgets are half the story — a scene can be trivially cheap to draw and still fail to load because its textures do not fit in VRAM.

assume_compressed.description: Report cost after KTX2/Basis transcoding (~8:1) instead of raw RGBA. Only set this once the cook step actually compresses, or the number is fiction

ops.name: image.analyze
ops.summary: Measure a concept image instead of eyeballing it: silhouette coverage and proportions, left-right symmetry, dominant and regional palette, and an honest recommendation — extrude it (image.to_mesh) or use it as parametric guidance for a recipe. The first step of concept art -> production asset.

path.description: Image file (PNG with alpha, or any subject on a fairly uniform background)

threshold.description: Background distance cutoff when there is no alpha channel; raise if the backdrop bleeds into the subject

ops.name: image.to_mesh
ops.summary: Turn a concept image into a real 3D solid: extract the subject silhouette, extrude it with a bevelled rim, and map the source image onto the front face as a texture (or bake it to vertex colours). Returns the silhouette IoU against the source — 'how close is the model to the picture' as a number, not a vibe. Emblems, totems, props, side-view creatures, relief work.

target_height.description: Silhouette height in metres; width follows the image aspect

depth.description: Extrusion depth in metres along the view axis

bevel.description: Rim chamfer — catches light so the edge reads; 0 disables

texture.description: project: map the source image on the front face; vertex: bake nearest pixel colours to COLOR_0; none: flat palette material

simplify.description: Contour simplification tolerance in working pixels — higher is fewer vertices and smoother shapes

seed.description: Random seed (reserved; the mesh is a pure function of the image)

ops.name: kit.piece
ops.summary: One modular kit piece with its origin at the grid corner, ready to snap. Build a whole set with kit.set instead if you want more than one.

grid.description: Grid module size in metres — use ONE value across the whole kit

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile — MUST match across the kit

detail.description: Extra edge loops for later greebling

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: kit.room
ops.summary: Assemble a closed room from kit pieces: floor, four walls with a door and windows, optional pillars and roof. Produces a playable space, not just parts.

size.description: Room size in grid modules [x, y]

doors.description: Number of doorway modules to cut into the walls

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile

join.description: Merge into one mesh (recommended — one draw call)

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: kit.set
ops.summary: Generate a complete, texel-consistent modular kit in one call — floor, walls, door, window, corner, pillar, stairs, roof. This is the fastest path from nothing to a level a designer can actually build with.

uv_scale.description: Shared metres-per-UV-tile across the whole set

layout.description: Lay the pieces out in a row for review rendering

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: material.bake
ops.summary: Bake procedural shading down to an image texture and rewire the material to use it. This is what makes procedural materials shippable.

samples.description: Cycles samples; 16 is plenty for base colour, raise for AO

unwrap.description: Auto-unwrap first — baking needs non-overlapping UVs

rewire.description: Replace the procedural graph with the baked texture

ops.name: material.bake_detail
ops.summary: Bake high-poly detail onto a low-poly mesh as a tangent-space normal (or AO) map. This is what makes a cheap mesh read as an expensive one: the silhouette stays low-poly but the surface gets its detail back. Use this instead of material.bake when the detail lives in a separate dense mesh -- material.bake bakes an object onto itself, so its normal pass just reproduces the low-poly's own flat normals.

low.description: Low-poly object that receives the texture (needs UVs)

high.description: High-poly source object(s) the detail is projected from

samples.description: Cycles samples; raise for AO, 32 is plenty for normals

cage_extrusion.description: Metres to push the low-poly out before casting rays

max_ray_distance.description: Metres to search for the high-poly surface

attach.description: Link the baked map into the low-poly's existing material

ops.name: material.bake_pbr
ops.summary: Bake a layered material into a real PBR texture set (base colour, normal, roughness, AO) and rewire it as glTF-safe image textures. This is the step that makes a procedurally-surfaced asset actually shippable.

stem.description: Filename stem (defaults to the object name)

samples.description: Cycles samples; AO and normal want more than base colour

unwrap.description: Auto-unwrap first — baking needs non-overlapping UVs

margin.description: Bake margin in pixels; prevents seams at low mips

ops.name: material.consolidate
ops.summary: Merge materials that render identically into one shared material. Composing a scene from many prop recipes leaves a pile of near-duplicate materials, and every distinct material is a draw call — this collapses them without changing how anything looks.

tolerance.description: How close two materials' colour/roughness/metallic must be to count as the same

objects.description: Limit to these objects (empty = whole scene)

dry_run.description: Report what would merge without changing anything

ops.name: material.detail_normal
ops.summary: Generate a surface-detail normal map procedurally (cloth weave, hide scales, skin pores, wood grain) and wire it into the object's material. Bake passes only capture GEOMETRY normals, so shader bumps never survive export — this writes the relief into a real normal map, which is what makes cloth/skin/hide read as material instead of flat plastic at close range. Deterministic (seeded), glTF-safe (TEX_IMAGE + NORMAL_MAP only).

pattern.description: Surface class: weave=cloth, scales=hide/armour, pores=skin/leather, grain=wood

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: material.face_assign
ops.summary: Give a subset of faces its own material — trim strips, emissive panels, painted details. Selected by world-space direction or height.

preset.description: Material preset for the selected faces

band_min.description: top_band/bottom_band: lower bound as a fraction of height. Bands select by face CENTER, so a thin band needs real face rows at that height - one tall quad (e.g. a column shaft) has its centre near the middle and a thin band elsewhere matches nothing

band_max.description: top_band/bottom_band: upper bound as a fraction of height

roughness.description: Override roughness 0..1; -1 keeps the preset value

metallic.description: Override metallic 0..1; -1 keeps the preset value. Metals read black without something bright to reflect - painted trim (metallic ~0.15) survives dark environments

ops.name: material.list
ops.summary: List materials in the file and flag any that glTF cannot export.

ops.name: material.pbr
ops.summary: Apply a layered AAA-grade surface: base albedo, curvature-driven EDGE WEAR, ambient-occlusion-driven CAVITY DIRT, two octaves of micro-detail and non-constant roughness. This is the single biggest jump in perceived quality — flat-coloured geometry never reads as AAA no matter how good the silhouette. Bake it with material.bake_pbr before export.

roughness.description: Mid roughness; the layers vary around it

detail_scale.description: Micro-detail frequency — higher is finer grain

grain.description: How strongly the noise tints the albedo

edge_wear.description: Abrasion on convex edges (0..1). Real objects are worn where they stick out

edge_color.description: Colour of worn edges; defaults to a lighter base

seed.description: Random seed for the noise

ops.name: material.procedural
ops.summary: Build a noise/voronoi/wave/gradient material. Gives surfaces real variation instead of flat colour — but it must be baked (material.bake) before it can export to glTF.

kind.description: Pattern type: noise=rock/dirt, voronoi=cracked stone/scales, wave=wood grain/strata, gradient=vertical fade, checker=UV debug

roughness.description: Base roughness; the pattern modulates around it

distortion.description: Warps the pattern; makes wood grain and marble believable

ops.name: material.set
ops.summary: Create and assign a PBR material. Prefer a preset name (stone, wood, metal, gold, crystal...) — the presets have physically sane roughness/metallic values.

preset.description: Material preset; see meta.palette for the list

color.description: Override colour: palette name, #rrggbb, or a linear [r,g,b] triple

roughness.description: Override roughness 0..1; -1 keeps the preset value

metallic.description: Override metallic 0..1; -1 keeps the preset value

emission.description: Emission strength; -1 keeps the preset value

ops.name: material.tileable
ops.summary: Bake a SEAMLESS PBR texture set and apply it repeating across a surface. This is how architecture gets textured: a unique bake for a 725 m stadium works out to ~3 px/m, which is no texture at all, whereas one 1k tiling map gives real surface detail everywhere. Noise is sampled through a torus mapping so it tiles perfectly with no visible seam.

detail_scale.description: Feature size in the baked map — higher is finer

dirt.description: Grime settled in the low spots (0..1)

tiles.description: How many times the map repeats across the object's UVs

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection; 0 keeps existing UVs

stem.description: Filename stem (defaults to the object name)

reuse.description: If this stem was already baked, assign the existing material instead of baking again. Bake once, apply to every stone surface in a building — same texture, one set of maps, one draw call

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: mesh.clean
ops.summary: Sweep a neural/scan mesh before retopo: delete floating islands below a size share of the main body, then Taubin-smooth the surface (smooth + counter-smooth, so it denoises without shrinking). Neural soup carries floaters and high-frequency noise that voxel retopo faithfully preserves — clean first or the spikes ship.

name.description: Mesh object to clean (modified in place)

island_min_share.description: Drop disconnected islands smaller than this fraction of the largest island's face count (0.02 = keep anything at least 2% of the main body)

smooth_iterations.description: Laplacian rounds — 1-3 denoises neural output; 0 keeps the raw surface

smooth_factor.description: Step size per round, capped at 0.35: a negative-volume counter-step (Taubin) was tried and SHREDDED voxel-quad meshes — plain small steps are the safe smooth

despike_iterations.description: Outlier-clamp passes — collapse verts sitting >threshold x the median edge length away from their neighbourhood median (the long thin spikes neural extraction leaves)

despike_threshold.description: Spike cutoff as a multiple of the median edge length

ops.name: mesh.retopo
ops.summary: Rebuild a dense triangle soup (neural/scan import) as a clean all-quad mesh via voxel remesh, in place. Robust on any input — open seams, overlapping shells, interior garbage all get swallowed by the voxel grid. Destroys UVs and skin weights (unwrap again after; re-rig if it had a rig). Pair with bake.transfer to move the source's textures and detail across.

name.description: Mesh object to retopologize (modified in place)

voxel_size.description: Voxel edge in metres — 0 picks it from the bounds (~1/120 of the longest side). Smaller keeps more detail at more quads

adaptivity.description: Quad adaptivity 0..0.2 — higher spends quads only where curvature demands

strip_rig.description: Retopo destroys skin weights: unparent, drop armature modifiers, and apply transforms first (neural/scan inputs arrive unrigged anyway)

ops.name: meta.help
ops.summary: Full parameter schema and defaults for one operation.

ops.name: meta.ops
ops.summary: List every available operation with its parameters. Call this first if you are unsure what exists.

tag.description: Filter by tag (session, build, prop, kit, env, char, gameready, render, export, check)

search.description: Filter by substring in the op name or summary

detail.description: How much to return per op

ops.name: meta.palette
ops.summary: The studio colour palette and material presets. Use these names instead of inventing colours — palette discipline is what makes a set of assets look like one game.

ops.name: morph.add
ops.summary: Add a shape key that displaces vertices by a deterministic rule — dent a crate for a damage state, inflate a cartoon prop, taper a tree trunk, bulge a cartoon cheek. Exports to glTF as a morph target on top of Basis.

name.description: Mesh object to add the shape key to

key.description: Shape key name — this becomes the glTF morph target name (extras.targetNames), so make it meaningful: 'dented', 'inflate', 'blink'

rule.description: Displacement rule: inflate pushes verts out along their normals, dent pulls verts inside `radius` toward `center`, bulge pushes them away, flatten squashes toward the center plane along `axis`, taper scales the cross-section down along `axis`

amount.description: Displacement in metres (flatten/taper: 0..1 fraction of the way)

axis.description: Axis for flatten and taper (z is up)

center.description: Local-space point the rule acts around; omit to use the centre of the mesh's own bounds

radius.description: Reach of the effect in metres — verts beyond this from `center` are untouched (taper: full axis half-extent)

falloff.description: How the effect fades toward `radius`; smooth eases out, linear is a straight ramp

ops.name: morph.animate
ops.summary: Keyframe a shape key's weight over time so glTF exports a morph-target animation channel — a crate denting on impact, a chest lid swell, a pulsing crystal. Follows the same action idiom as char.animate.

name.description: Mesh object with the shape key

frames.description: Frame numbers, e.g. [1, 12, 24]; must be the same length as `values`

values.description: Weight at each frame (0..1), e.g. [0, 1, 0] pops the morph and settles back

ops.name: morph.list
ops.summary: Report an object's shape keys: names, slider ranges and current values. Check this before morph.animate — the key name must match exactly.

ops.name: morph.set
ops.summary: Set a shape key's slider value (0..1) for review renders — pose the dent at 60% before render.contact_sheet so the still shows the damaged state.

name.description: Mesh object with the shape key

key.description: Shape key name (from morph.add or morph.list)

value.description: Slider weight, clamped to 0..1: 0 is Basis, 1 is the full morph

ops.name: object.delete
ops.summary: Remove objects from the scene.

ops.name: object.duplicate
ops.summary: Copy an object, optionally placing the copy in one call.

new_name.description: Name for the copy (auto-derived when empty)

ops.name: object.inspect
ops.summary: Detailed report for one object: topology, UV quality, texel density, materials, bounds.

texture_size.description: Texture resolution used for the texel-density figure

ops.name: object.join
ops.summary: Merge several meshes into one object, de-duplicating material slots. Fewer objects means fewer draw calls.

names.description: Objects to merge (the first one's transform wins)

ops.name: object.list
ops.summary: List object names in the scene, optionally filtered by a name prefix.

prefix.description: Only return names starting with this

ops.name: object.origin
ops.summary: Set an object's pivot. Use 'bottom' for floor props, 'center' for pickups, 'world' for modular kit pieces.

ops.name: object.parent
ops.summary: Parent one object to another, keeping the child's world transform. Entity hierarchy is how World IR parts become a GLB node tree.

ops.name: object.rename
ops.summary: Rename an object, coercing the new name to the studio's snake_case convention.

ops.name: object.shade
ops.summary: Set smooth or flat shading. Smooth shading with an angle threshold is what makes curved props read as curved.

angle.description: Edges sharper than this angle (degrees) stay hard

ops.name: object.transform
ops.summary: Move, rotate or scale an object. Rotation is in degrees.

apply.description: Bake rotation+scale into mesh data (required before export)

ops.name: paint.cavity
ops.summary: Bake 'dirt in the crevices' or 'edge wear' without textures: a deterministic geometric curvature estimate per vertex. Concave spots (recesses, grooves, inside corners) take the colour in cavity mode; convex ridges take it in edge mode. Blends over the existing layer, so fill white first if the mesh is unpainted.

name.description: Mesh object to paint — needs real surface relief; a flat quad has no curvature to find

color.description: Colour blended into the crevices/edges: palette name, #rrggbb, or linear [r,g,b]. Dark browns read as grime, light greys as worn edges

mode.description: cavity paints concave spots (dirt), edge paints convex ridges (wear)

strength.description: Blend strength multiplier; the deepest cavity gets the full colour at 1.0

invert.description: Flip the result — paint everything EXCEPT the crevices/edges

layer.description: Colour attribute name; the glTF exporter ships the active one as COLOR_0

ops.name: paint.fill
ops.summary: Set every loop of a mesh to one vertex colour. The base coat for the other paint.* ops — fill white before paint.cavity so unpainted areas stay neutral, or fill a flat tint for a stylised asset.

color.description: Colour: palette name, #rrggbb, or linear [r,g,b]. White leaves the material unchanged when the engine multiplies COLOR_0 in

layer.description: Colour attribute name; the glTF exporter ships the active one as COLOR_0

ops.name: paint.height
ops.summary: Paint a two-colour gradient along an axis — dust at the base of a wall, a snow line on a peak, waterline grime on a hull. Cheaper than any texture and it can never stretch or seam.

low.description: Colour at the bottom of the range: palette name, #rrggbb, or linear [r,g,b]

high.description: Colour at the top of the range

axis.description: Axis the gradient runs along (z is up). Measured in the mesh's LOCAL space, like material.face_assign

min.description: Axis value for 100% `low`; omit to use the mesh's own lower bound. Set both min and max to share one gradient across several objects

max.description: Axis value for 100% `high`; omit to use the mesh's upper bound

curve.description: Gradient easing; smooth eases in and out, which hides the band edges

layer.description: Colour attribute name; the glTF exporter ships the active one as COLOR_0

ops.name: paint.noise
ops.summary: Blend two colours by deterministic fBm noise sampled at vertex positions — mottled wear, rust patches, moss, dirt variation. Breaks up flat fills so large surfaces stop looking computer-perfect.

color_a.description: Colour where the noise is low: palette name, #rrggbb, or linear [r,g,b]

color_b.description: Colour where the noise is high

scale.description: Noise frequency in 1/metres — higher gives smaller, busier patches

seed.description: Random seed; same seed gives the same pattern forever

octaves.description: Fractal detail levels; more octaves, finer grain

layer.description: Colour attribute name; the glTF exporter ships the active one as COLOR_0

ops.name: prop.banner
ops.summary: Hanging banner or flag with a cloth wave. ~180 tris. Cheap way to add faction identity and colour to grey architecture.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

size.description: Cloth width and drop in metres

ops.name: prop.barrel
ops.summary: Lathed barrel with a belly and iron bands. ~500 tris. Bands get their own material slot so they can read as metal.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

belly.description: How much the middle bulges (0 = straight cylinder)

open_top.description: Hollow out the top (for water butts, planters)

ops.name: prop.chest
ops.summary: Treasure chest with a curved lid, iron banding and a lock plate. ~700 tris. Lid is a separate object so it can be hinged and animated.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

size.description: Base dimensions (lid adds height on top)

separate_lid.description: Keep the lid as its own object for hinge animation

ops.name: prop.crate
ops.summary: Wooden crate with a recessed-panel frame. ~350 tris. The frame is what makes it read as a crate rather than a box.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

planks.description: Horizontal plank divisions per panel (0 for plain)

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile

ops.name: prop.crystal
ops.summary: Crystal cluster: several tapered prisms fanned from a common base. ~300 tris. Emissive by default — reads as a light source and a landmark.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

spread.description: Maximum lean from vertical, in degrees

ops.name: prop.debris
ops.summary: Scattered rubble field: broken stone, planks and dust chunks around a point. ~50 tris per piece. Turns a clean floor into a fought-over one.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: prop.fence
ops.summary: Fence run with posts and rails. ~40 tris per metre. Blocks player movement and sells scale better than almost any other cheap prop.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: prop.furniture
ops.summary: Table, bench, stool, shelf or bed frame. ~200 tris. The set dressing that makes an interior look inhabited.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: prop.pillar
ops.summary: Classical column: base, tapered shaft, capital, optional fluting. ~600 tris. Instant architecture.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: prop.rock
ops.summary: Irregular rock with a flat base so it sits on the ground instead of floating. ~200 tris at detail 2. The single most reused environment prop in any game.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

flatten_base.description: Cut a flat bottom so it beds into terrain

ops.name: prop.sack
ops.summary: Cloth sack, cinched at the neck. ~400 tris. Good filler for markets, camps and storerooms.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

slump.description: How much the body sags and spreads at the base

ops.name: prop.torch
ops.summary: Wall torch or standing brazier with an emissive flame. ~250 tris. Emissive props double as level-design landmarks.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: prop.tree
ops.summary: Stylised low-poly tree: tapered trunk plus layered canopy. ~450 tris. Canopy is a separate material slot so it can take a foliage/alpha shader.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

lean.description: Trunk lean in degrees — a perfectly vertical tree looks fake

ops.name: prop.weapon
ops.summary: Sword, axe, spear, hammer or shield built from a blade/haft/grip breakdown. ~400 tris. Pivot sits at the grip so it parents straight to a hand bone.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: render.camera
ops.summary: Render from an explicit camera position and target. Auto-framing always fits the WHOLE subject, which is useless on a 700 m stadium or a 40 m terrain — this is how you get a close-up, an eye-level gameplay view, or a hero shot.

position.description: Camera position in metres. This op exists to place the camera by hand; use render.cinematic or render.view when you want the framing fitted for you

lens.description: Focal length in mm — 24 is wide, 50 neutral, 105 compressed

aspect.description: Width / height. Use 1.78 for a 16:9 gameplay framing

light_distance.description: Light rig scale in metres; 0 fits it to the whole scene

world_light.description: Ambient dome strength. Higher fills shadows but piles white specular sheen onto every surface, which washes out saturated albedo

ops.name: render.cinematic
ops.summary: A film-grade beauty render: physical sun and sky, global illumination, atmospheric haze, depth of field and a filmic tonemap. render.view and render.camera are flat REVIEW rigs built to judge albedo honestly; this one is built to show the asset at its best, and it is the render that tells you whether the art actually holds up.

position.description: Camera position in metres. Omit it and a three-quarter beauty angle is fitted to the subject — set it for a close-up or a specific composition

target.description: Point to look at. When both camera position and target are omitted, the camera aims at the subject's own centre so assets built off-origin are still framed. An explicit position with no target keeps the established world-origin target

samples.description: Path-tracing samples. This is a beauty render; it costs time

sun_energy.description: Sun strength in W/m2. 3-6 reads as hard daylight

sun_angle.description: Sun elevation and azimuth in degrees. Low sun = long shadows

sun_color.description: Sunlight colour; warmer at low elevation

sky_color.description: Zenith sky colour, which is also the fill light

haze.description: Volumetric atmosphere density. 0.0005-0.004 separates distant forms; costs render time

focus.description: Depth of field focus distance; 0 measures it to the target

aperture.description: f-stop. 0 disables depth of field. 2.8 is shallow, 8 is deep

bounces.description: Light bounces. GI is most of what makes a render look expensive

look.description: View transform. Filmic/AgX roll off highlights like film; standard clips them

ops.name: render.contact_sheet
ops.summary: THE review image. Renders hero/front/side/top plus a wireframe pass (shows topology and wasted triangles) and a checker pass (shows UV stretch and texel-density mismatches), composited into one PNG. Look at this after generating anything — it is how you catch problems a triangle count cannot show.

ops.name: render.impostor
ops.summary: Bake an object into a billboard impostor sprite sheet: N orthographic views orbiting it, packed left-to-right then top-to-bottom into ONE transparent PNG, plus a JSON sidecar (grid layout, yaw angles, bounds) with everything a game engine needs to billboard it. This is THE distant-LOD technique — swap the real mesh for a camera-facing quad with this sheet beyond a few hundred metres and a browser can show thousands of instances at full frame rate. Pass normals=True to also bake a world-space normal sheet so the billboard can react to scene lighting.

name.description: Object to bake; its children are baked with it. Use object.list if you are unsure of the exact name

out.description: Sprite-sheet PNG path. The JSON sidecar is written next to it as <stem>.json

views.description: Yaw angles around the object, evenly spaced over 360 degrees. 8 is the standard for props; 4 is enough for near-symmetric ones and halves the bake time

size.description: Pixel size of each frame (frames are square). Billboards are only ever seen at distance, so 64-256 is the useful range — bigger just costs render time

normals.description: Also write <stem>_normal.png: world-space normals packed into 0..1 colour, so the billboard can be lit instead of looking pasted on. Doubles render cost

samples.description: Cycles samples per frame. 16 is plenty at these sizes; raise only if the sprites look grainy

elevation.description: Camera height above the horizon in degrees, the same for every view. Ground props read best at 0-15; high values waste frame area on the top face

ops.name: render.sprite
ops.summary: Render a GAME ICON, not a screenshot: silhouette-safe shared framing on a long lens, a warm-key/cool-fill/bright-kicker rig anchored to the camera so a whole set matches, a real contact shadow, supersampled edges, a radial backdrop or clean alpha, and a linear-light post chain (highlight bloom, ACES tonemap, grade, vignette). Pass views>1 for a directional sheet with stable world scale and ground anchor at every angle.

name.description: Object to shoot; its children come with it. Omit to frame every mesh in the scene

out.description: PNG output path. With views>1 a <stem>.json sidecar describing the grid is written next to it

size.description: Output size in pixels per square frame, clamped to 32-2048. Sheet dimensions participate in the aggregate resource preflight; 256-1024 is the useful icon range

supersample.description: Render each axis at 1-4x then area-downsample in premultiplied linear light for cleaner silhouette edges. The internal render is capped at 4096 px per axis and all supersampled pixels participate in the resource preflight

views.description: How many yaw angles to shoot, clamped to 1-64. 1 is an icon; 8 or 16 packs a stable-scale directional sheet. Every view participates in the aggregate resource preflight

azimuth.description: Camera compass angle in degrees. -47 is the standard three-quarter view that shows a front and a side at once

elevation.description: Camera height above the horizon in degrees. 20-30 reads as 'held up in front of you'; 45+ becomes a map marker

lens.description: Focal length in mm. Long lenses flatten perspective, which is why product and icon work uses them — 85-135 keeps the far side of the object from tapering away

fill.description: Fraction of the frame the subject spans at its widest. Hold this constant across a set and the icons line up; that is the whole trick

background.description: gradient is a radial backdrop that separates the silhouette everywhere; alpha leaves it transparent for compositing into a UI; solid is a flat fill

bg_outer.description: Backdrop colour at the corners (gradient only)

key_color.description: Key light colour — warm reads as sunlight

fill_color.description: Fill light colour — cool reads as sky, and the warm/cool split is most of what makes a surface look lit rather than painted

rim_color.description: Kicker colour; the light that draws the silhouette

rim.description: Kicker strength. 0 turns separation off, 1.5-2 is a hero/legendary treatment

key_energy.description: Key light strength multiplier. 1.0 puts an 18% grey card near the top of the mid-tones, which is where an icon wants to sit

fill_energy.description: Fill light strength multiplier. Raise it when the analysis reports crushed shadows — the shadow side of a three-quarter view is half the icon

exposure.description: Exposure compensation in stops, clamped to -16..16 and applied in linear light before the tonemap

bloom.description: Highlight glow strength. 0 disables it; above ~0.8 the asset starts to dissolve

bloom_threshold.description: Linear luminance a pixel must exceed to bloom

contrast.description: Contrast multiplier about mid-grey, applied after the tonemap

saturation.description: Saturation multiplier. Stylised game icons run hot; 1.0 is neutral

vignette.description: Corner darkening. Ignored when background=alpha, which must stay compositable

look.description: Tonemap. aces is the film-style curve games ship; punchy adds saturation in the curve; linear clips, for data

shadow.description: Cast a real contact shadow onto an invisible ground plane so the subject sits on something

samples.description: Path-tracing samples, clamped to 8-256 and charged per supersampled pixel/view by the aggregate resource preflight. Icons are small and seen close; 96-256 is the honest range

ops.name: render.turntable
ops.summary: Render an orbit of frames around the subject. Use when a single angle cannot settle whether a silhouette works.

ops.name: render.view
ops.summary: Render one framed view of the scene or of specific objects. The camera and a three-point light rig are auto-fitted to the subject, so you never get an empty or blown-out frame.

objects.description: Objects to frame and show (empty = whole scene)

samples.description: Render samples — 24 is enough to judge form

engine.description: Render engine. 'auto' means Cycles/CPU, which is the only one that works without a GPU context; 'eevee' is faster but crashes headless on machines with no display server

world_light.description: Ambient dome strength. Higher fills shadows but piles white specular sheen onto every surface, which washes out saturated albedo

ops.name: rig.keyframe
ops.summary: Author an animation clip from explicit per-frame bone poses. Give the poses that define the motion and let the interpolation do the rest — this is how a real cycle is built, not by driving bones with sine waves.

keys.description: {"1": {"spine": [rx, ry, rz]}, "12": {...}} — frame -> bone -> XYZ degrees

locations.description: Optional {"frame": {"bone": [x, y, z]}} bone translations in metres

loop.description: Match the last frame to the first so the clip cycles seamlessly

ops.name: rig.mirror_bones
ops.summary: Duplicate a set of bones mirrored across an axis, renaming _l to _r (or vice versa). Halves the work of describing a symmetrical skeleton.

bones.description: Bone specs to mirror, same shape as rig.skeleton

ops.name: rig.skeleton
ops.summary: Build an armature from an explicit bone list — any creature, not just humanoids. Each bone is {name, head:[x,y,z], tail:[x,y,z], parent}. Exactly one bone may be parentless, because engines and the studio validator both require a single root.

ops.name: rig.skin
ops.summary: Bind a mesh to an armature using distance-to-bone falloff weights. Works on any skeleton and never fails the way Blender's bone-heat solver does on a non-watertight mesh.

falloff.description: Weight sharpness; higher is more rigid, lower is smoother

influences.description: Bones influencing each vertex (2 is right for game skins)

only_bones.description: Restrict binding to these bones (empty = all deform bones)

ops.name: session.import
ops.summary: Import an existing glTF/GLB, OBJ, FBX or .blend into the current scene. Use this to inspect, critique, fix or extend assets a game already ships — not just ones you generated.

prefix.description: Rename imported objects with this prefix (keeps names snake_case)

location.description: Offset to place the import at

ops.name: session.info
ops.summary: Full scene report: every object with triangle counts, materials, UVs and bounds. Cheap; call it often.

ops.name: session.open
ops.summary: Load an existing .blend so you can inspect, fix or extend an asset instead of rebuilding it.

ops.name: session.reset
ops.summary: Clear the scene to a deterministic empty metric-unit state. Start every new asset with this.

unit_scale.description: Blender unit scale; keep 1.0 = 1 metre for game engines

ops.name: session.restore
ops.summary: Roll the scene back to a snapshot taken earlier in this session.

ops.name: session.save
ops.summary: Write the scene to a .blend master file (the committed source of truth in ADR 0006).

path.description: Output .blend path; relative paths land under the output dir

ops.name: session.snapshot
ops.summary: Save an in-memory scene checkpoint you can roll back to. Take one before any risky or destructive edit.

ops.name: uv.lightmap
ops.summary: Add a second, non-overlapping UV channel for baked lighting. Godot and Unity both require this for static lightmaps.

name.description: Name of the new UV layer

margin.description: Island padding — lightmaps need more than base textures

ops.name: uv.normalize
ops.summary: Fit existing UVs into the 0..1 square, preserving proportions.

ops.name: uv.pack
ops.summary: Repack existing UV islands into 0..1 without re-unwrapping. Use after joining objects or editing seams.

ops.name: uv.report
ops.summary: Measure UV quality: texel density, coverage, island count, overlap. Texel density is the number to match across an asset set — mismatched density is the most common reason AI-made assets look wrong together.

texture_size.description: Texture resolution the density figure assumes

ops.name: uv.unwrap
ops.summary: Generate UVs. Use 'box' with a shared uv_scale for anything using a tiling or trim texture (keeps texel density uniform across a whole kit); use 'smart_packed' for props that need their own baked texture.

scale.description: box only: metres per UV tile. Use the SAME value across a kit

margin.description: smart only: island padding, prevents bleed at low mip levels
